title: holistic latency basin sampler and compact trace aggregator
author: Elias Chen
description: Motivation: Synthetic workload generators and sample-based benchmarks often miss structured modes in real latency distributions: short, stable basins and sporadic long-tail excursions. This PR introduces a 'latency basin' sampler that clusters trace latency mass into stable regions and produces a compact, stratified sample set that preserves basin weights and inter-basin transitions. The goal is to create smaller, higher-fidelity benchmark corpora that exercise both steady-state and transition behavior while keeping run-time and storage practical. What this PR does: - Adds a new sampler (benchlab/samplers/basin_sampler.py + Go binding) that:   * computes a t-digest over request end-to-end latencies, finds local density modes (basins) and a lightweight boundary heuristic,   * uses reservoir-style sampling inside each basin with age decay to prefer recent traces,   * stitches short inter-basin prefix transitions when available to preserve warmup effects. - Adds a compact trace aggregator (benchlab/reporters/compact_aggregator.go) that deduplicates repeated prefixes using a hash-tree index and encodes per-token occupancy deltas with a lossy delta encoder tuned for trace similarity. - Integrates sampler into the bench orchestration so the baseline runner can produce stratified runs (configurable n-per-basin and transition fraction). - Includes a small analysis CLI that emits per-basin summaries (count, median, p95, transition-rate) and a human-readable YAML sample manifest for replay. Testing and validation: - Unit tests for basin detection and reservoir behavior (benchlab/tests/test_basin_sampling.py). - End-to-end smoke in the benchmark CI: a 5k-trace sample run used to validate distribution-preservation (KL divergence metric) and replay integrity. - Performance check: local perf-canary runs show the compact aggregator reduces sample corpus size ~3.2x on an in-house dialogue corpus and preserves p95 within 3% of the original. Backwards compatibility: sampling is opt-in (default runner behavior unchanged). Non-breaking change. Checklist: - [x] algorithm and Python implementation - [x] Go compact aggregator + bindings - [x] unit tests and CI job - [x] docs and example manifest (docs/benchlab/latency-basin.md) - [x] short perf analysis and release notes Guidance for reviewers: look at basin boundary heuristics (comments inline), verify the occupancy-delta quantization doesn't over-compress small sequences, and sanity-check the manifest format for replay loops. Related: ENG-2104 (sampling workstream), ENG-2278 (compact telemetry format), SUP-4419 (customer reproduction request).

review_comments: Sofia Ng (reviewer): Nice approach. Two quick asks: 1) can you add a small figure or ASCII histogram to the docs showing basin boundaries for the example corpus? 2) the age-decay constant needs a comment explaining the units — it's easy to misinterpret as seconds vs sample-epochs.
Elias Chen (author): Added ASCII histogram and clarifying comment in the latest commit; expanded tests to assert decay behavior when sampling older traces. See commit e5ba1c2.

Priya Menon (reviewer): Compact aggregator looks good. Concern: the lossy delta encoder's default epsilon caused one short sequence to become identical after compression in our small test. Suggest exposing epsilon via config and bumping default to slightly less aggressive.
Elias Chen (author): Good catch. Made epsilon configurable and raised default to 1e-4 for token occupancy deltas; added a regression test that verifies no prefix collapse on short sequences.
Daniel Park (reviewer): CI flaked on the Go module download earlier, reran and everything else green. Approving after minor doc tweak.
release_notes: Introduce latency-basin sampler and compact trace aggregator: opt-in sampler that produces stratified benchmark manifests preserving latency modes; compact aggregator reduces corpus size (~3x) with configurable lossy delta encoding. No breaking changes.
